subject: Russian (Leaving Certificate, Higher Level only)
exam: Oral, aural and a written paper. The official papers are not included: the learner brings the question text from their own copy.

topics.title: Vocabulary about yourself: family, home, school, free time
recallPrompts: Say three sentences about each of your family members: who they are, what they do, what they are like.
Describe your home and your room in five sentences without looking at your list.
Name ten words for school subjects, school life and your daily routine.
Say what you do in your free time and how often, using three different adverbs of frequency.

topics.title: Oral: general conversation about yourself and your life (narrative)
recallPrompts: Introduce yourself in one minute: name, age, family, where you live, school, interests.
Tell the story of a recent weekend in the past tense, with at least five events in order.
Say what you plan to do after school, using the future tense and giving a reason.
Say one thing you are proud of and one thing you find difficult, with a reason for each.

topics.title: Noun cases: six cases, singular and plural, endings and spelling rules
recallPrompts: List the six cases and the question each one answers.
Decline one masculine, one feminine and one neuter noun in the singular, in all six cases.
Which case follows a negative, and which follows a number from two to four?
Give the plural of five nouns, including two irregular ones.
Which spelling rules change an ending after a hushing consonant or after a velar consonant?

topics.title: Verbs: conjugation, past, present and future, reflexive verbs
recallPrompts: Conjugate one first-conjugation and one second-conjugation verb in the present tense.
How do you form the past tense, and how does it agree with the subject?
How do you form the future of an imperfective verb and of a perfective verb?
Give the present tense of two verbs with a consonant change and explain the pattern.
How does a reflexive verb change in the present and in the past?

topics.title: Adjectives, possessives and pronouns: agreement in gender, number and case
recallPrompts: Write a noun phrase with an adjective in each of the six cases.
How do possessive and demonstrative words agree with the noun they describe?
How do you say "my" and "your" with a reflexive meaning, and when do you use it?
When do you use the short form of an adjective, and how is it formed?

topics.title: Vocabulary for wider topics: health, travel, work, environment, technology
recallPrompts: Give six words or phrases on health and the body, and use two in sentences.
Give six words or phrases on travel and transport, and use two in sentences.
Give six words or phrases on the environment or technology, and use two in sentences.
Give six words or phrases on work and money, and use two in sentences.
Say your opinion on one current issue using two phrases for giving an opinion.

topics.title: Language awareness: dictionary forms, parts of speech and cases
recallPrompts: Give the infinitive of five verbs you have met in the past tense, and say which are perfective.
Name the six cases in Russian and in English, with one question word for each.
Which five parts of speech does a language awareness task use, and how do you tell a noun from an adjective?

topics.title: Verb aspect: perfective and imperfective
recallPrompts: What is the difference between an imperfective and a perfective verb? Give one pair.
Which aspect do you use for repeated or ongoing actions, and which for a single completed action?
Which aspect usually follows words meaning "begin", "continue" and "finish"?
Which aspect do you choose in a negative command, and why?

topics.title: Prepositions and the cases they take
recallPrompts: List five prepositions that take the accusative and five that take the prepositional case.
Which prepositions take more than one case, and how does the meaning change?
How do you say "to", "at" and "from" with places and with people?
Which prepositions take the genitive case? Give three examples in sentences.

topics.title: Reading comprehension: detail questions and summary writing
recallPrompts: What do you do in the first two minutes with a new passage, before answering any question?
How can you guess the meaning of a new word from its root, its prefix or its context?
How do you make sure you give as many different details as the question asks for, and not the same one twice?
When you summarise a segment in a paragraph, how do you tell the essential information from the secondary details?

topics.title: Oral: everyday life in Ireland and in a Russian-speaking community
recallPrompts: Describe a typical day in Ireland and one difference from daily life in a Russian-speaking community.
Say what you like and what you would change about your town or area.
Give two points about being a young person in Ireland today, with an example for each.
Compare school life in Ireland with school life in a Russian-speaking country in four sentences.

topics.title: Verbs of motion and their prefixes
recallPrompts: List the pairs of unprefixed verbs of motion and say what distinguishes the two verbs in a pair.
Which verb of the pair do you use for one direction, and which for habitual or round trips?
List five motion prefixes and the meaning each one adds.
Make five sentences using a prefixed verb of motion with the right preposition and case.
How do verbs of motion work for people and for transport?

topics.title: Numerals, dates, time and quantity
recallPrompts: Say today’s date, your date of birth and the year in full, in the correct cases.
How do you tell the time on the hour, the half hour and at other times?
How does a noun change after one, after two to four, and after five or more?
How do you express age, quantity and approximate amounts?

topics.title: Cultural awareness: geography and general facts about Russia
recallPrompts: Give five facts about the geography of a Russian-speaking country.
Name three writers, artists or composers and one work by each.
Describe two festivals or traditions and when they are celebrated.
Give three facts about the history of a Russian-speaking country, with dates.
Describe one traditional dish and one custom around meals.

topics.title: Culture: cities, sights and tourism
recallPrompts: Name five Russian cities and one sight in each.
Describe Moscow or St Petersburg in five facts without looking at notes.
What can a tourist see on the Golden Ring or the Trans-Siberian railway?
Which places are on the UNESCO World Heritage list in Russia? Name three.

topics.title: Culture: nature, climate and animals
recallPrompts: Name six animals of Russia and where each one lives (taiga, tundra, Arctic, Far East).
Describe the climate of Russia and the different regions in five facts.
Name three lakes, rivers or mountains of Russia, with one fact about each.
What are the threats to the animal world and what can people do?

topics.title: Culture: writers, composers, artists and scientists
recallPrompts: Name three Russian writers and one work by each, and say what it is about.
Name two composers and two works, and two painters and two paintings.
Give three facts about one great Russian figure that you could put into a short essay.

topics.title: Culture: education, sport, family and everyday life
recallPrompts: Describe the school system in Russia in five facts and compare it with Ireland.
Name four popular sports in Russia and say where they are played or held.
Say five facts about family life and homes in Russia.

topics.title: Culture: festivals, food and fairy tales
recallPrompts: Describe how Russians celebrate New Year: who, what, when, what they eat.
Say five facts about Maslenitsa or another holiday.
Retell one Russian fairy tale in five sentences, in the past tense.
Name five traditional dishes and say what each is made of.

topics.title: Oral: aspects of culture in a Russian-speaking community
recallPrompts: Talk for two minutes about one aspect of culture you can speak about with confidence.
Give an opinion about a work of art, a book or a film connected with a Russian-speaking country, with reasons.
Explain one tradition and why it matters to people.
What follow-up question might the examiner ask you on this, and how would you answer?

topics.title: Oral: the project (presentation and questions)
recallPrompts: Present your project in one minute: the topic, why you chose it and three main facts.
List ten words you need for your project topic and use each in a sentence.
Say what you learned, in the past tense, and what you would still like to find out, in the future.
Write down three questions an examiner could ask about your project and answer each aloud.

topics.title: Linking ideas: conjunctions, relative clauses, participles, reported speech
recallPrompts: List five conjunctions that join two ideas, and say whether each adds, contrasts or gives a reason.
Form a relative clause and explain how its case is chosen.
Turn a direct statement and a direct question into reported speech.
Join two short sentences using a participle or a verbal adverb.

topics.title: Structuring discourse: matching and organising short texts
recallPrompts: How do you decide which newspaper section a short news item belongs to? Name the key words that give it away for three sections.
List five linking phrases and where each fits in a text: beginning, contrast, reason, result, ending.
Which words show that one sentence refers back to the one before?

topics.title: Oral: aspects of contemporary life in a Russian-speaking community
recallPrompts: Talk for two minutes about a contemporary issue young people face, with one example.
Give two advantages and two disadvantages of social media.
Say how life for young people has changed in the last twenty years, using the past and the present.
Explain your view on one social or environmental problem, with a reason and an example.

topics.title: Written expression with grammar: putting words into the correct form in a text
recallPrompts: In a text with words in brackets, what do you check for each one: case, gender and number, tense, or aspect?
Which grammar points do you most often get wrong in a short written task? List three and the rule for each.
Write three sentences that each show a different tense and a different case.
How do you check a piece of writing for endings and agreement in two minutes?

topics.title: Short essay on Russian culture: about 50 words with five facts
recallPrompts: Plan a short essay of about 50 words on a cultural topic: a title, five factual details and a short ending.
Give three phrases for giving a fact and three for giving your opinion.
Name two cultural topics for which you could write ten sentences without notes.

topics.title: Guided writing: letter, narrative or discussion
recallPrompts: List the parts of an informal letter: how it begins, how it ends and what goes between.
List the parts of a narrative: setting, events, high point, ending. Which tense will you use?
List the parts of a discussion: your view, two arguments with examples, the other side, your conclusion.
Give three ways to be sure you have covered every point the task asks for.

topics.title: Imperative, conditional, comparatives and superlatives
recallPrompts: Form the imperative of three verbs: informal, formal and plural.
How do you form a conditional sentence and a wish?
Form the comparative of five adjectives in two different ways.
How do you form the superlative, and how do you say "than"?

topics.title: Aural: listening for gist and detail
recallPrompts: What do you do in the first listening and what do you do in the second?
Which numbers, dates and times are easy to mix up, and how can you check them?
How do you note down a name or an unfamiliar word in a few seconds?

topics.title: Accuracy: spelling, stress, punctuation and proofreading
recallPrompts: List the spelling rules that cause most of your mistakes and write one example for each.
Which punctuation rules for commas in compound and complex sentences do you know?
Where does the stress fall in five words you often mispronounce?

checkProfiles.label: Short essay on culture (about 50 words)
criteria: There is a title; a missing title loses a mark.
There are five different facts about the topic. List each fact I gave and say which one is weak or repeated.
An introductory remark counts for at most one fact.
Language: endings, tenses, spelling and word order, with the rule for each error.

checkProfiles.label: Guided writing: letter, narrative or discussion (about 140 words)
criteria: Every point of the task is covered; list each point and where I covered it. At least one point from each category must appear.
Language: endings, aspect, verb forms, vocabulary and spelling, including the soft sign.
Textual coherence: the text hangs together with linking words, the right register and a clear beginning and ending.
I did not copy phrases word for word from the paper.

checkProfiles.label: Comprehension answers (in English)
criteria: Each answer gives the number of different details the question asks for; point out any that give too few or repeat the same detail.
The answer is in the language the paper asks for, which is English for most questions.
A summary paragraph has four details from the text and is in my own words.

checkProfiles.label: Transcript of what I said (oral)
criteria: I answered the question that was asked and added a reason or an opinion.
I used the past, present and future where they fit.
The language is natural spoken Russian: cases after prepositions, verb forms and linking words.

pastPaperPointers.note: Own-words descriptions of where each exam part sits in the official Higher papers.

comprehension.text: Q1 is Vadim's personal letter about school progress, sport, class events and home life, with detail questions plus cases and a short cultural-awareness note. Q2 is a four-voice survey on women in society, followed by verb infinitives and a family semantic field.

Choice year: Q1 is a blog profile of teenage singer Liza, with detail questions plus either noun cases or a music semantic field. Q2 is four teenagers discussing career choices, followed by verb infinitives or parts of speech.

Choice year: Q1 follows budget-travel writer Roman, with detail questions plus either verb infinitives or parts of speech. Q2 is four accounts of studying Russian or attending Russian universities, followed by a higher-education semantic field or noun cases.

Q1 is a last-day-of-school friendship story about Denis and Kolya, with detail questions plus either verb infinitives or noun cases. Q2 gives four gifted-child profiles, followed by parts of speech or a music semantic field from section 1.

Q1 is a Paustovsky cat story about the village thief becoming a household guardian, with detail questions plus either verb infinitives or parts of speech. Q2 gives four views on teenage work, followed by an employment semantic field or noun cases.

Q1 explains the Last Bell school-leaving tradition and compares it with Ireland, with detail questions plus an education semantic field or parts of speech. Q2 is a four-voice text on language learning and bilingualism, followed by verb infinitives or noun cases.

Q1 is a winter adventure story about Seryozhka, Jack the dog and a rediscovered garage, with detail questions plus verb infinitives or a winter semantic field. Q2 summarises four graduates' first-summer plans, then offers parts of speech or noun cases.

Match 10 brief news items to 10 newspaper sections.
